blocks.prompt: 19. If \(a_k\) and \(a_m\) denote two different terms of an A.P., show that its \(n^{\text{th}}\) term is \(a_k + (n - k)\left(\frac{a_k - a_m}{k - m}\right)\).
blocks.explanation:
A proof. We want a formula for \(a_n\) that uses the \(k\)th and \(m\)th terms instead of \(a_1\).
Plan: find \(d\) from the two terms; then go from \(a_k\) to \(a_n\) in \((n - k)\) steps of \(d\).
steps:
Given: \(a_k\) and \(a_m\) are terms of an A.P. (\(k \ne m\))
To prove: \(a_n = a_k + (n - k)\dfrac{a_k - a_m}{k - m}\).
Method: \(a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d\) for \(n = k\) and \(n = m\).

Write the two terms
\[a_k = a_1 + (k - 1)d \quad (1)\]
\[a_m = a_1 + (m - 1)d \quad (2)\]
Why: The general term with \(n = k\) and \(n = m\).

Subtract to find \(d\)
\[a_k - a_m = (k - m)d\]
\[d = \dfrac{a_k - a_m}{k - m}\]
Why: \(a_1\) cancels and \((k - 1) - (m - 1) = k - m\). Since the terms are different, \(k \ne m\).

Relate \(a_n\) to \(a_k\)
\[a_n - a_k = [a_1 + (n - 1)d]\]
\[\quad - [a_1 + (k - 1)d]\]
\[= (n - k)d\]
Why: Same idea: subtracting removes \(a_1\).

Substitute \(d\)
\[a_n = a_k + (n - k)d\]
\[= a_k + (n - k)\dfrac{a_k - a_m}{k - m}\]
Why: Put the value of \(d\) found above.

Check
\(n = m\): \(a_k + (m - k)\dfrac{a_k - a_m}{k - m} = a_k - (a_k - a_m) = a_m \;\checkmark\)
Why: \(\frac{m - k}{k - m} = -1\), so the formula gives back \(a_m\).
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(a_n = a_k + (n - k)\left(\frac{a_k - a_m}{k - m}\right)\).
